name: Huntr
subcategory: resumes, job tracking and interview practice
tagline: Track job applications, contacts, tasks, documents, and tailored materials in one workspace

tiers.name: Free
tiers.limits: Unlimited base resumes; 2 tailored resumes; 2 application packets; track 100 jobs; 100 document uploads.

tiers.name: Pro
tiers.limits: Unlimited tailored resumes, application packets, AI usage, tracked jobs and document uploads.
tiers.notes: Also sold quarterly for $90 ($30/month equivalent) and for 6 months at $160 ($26.67/month equivalent).

pricing.freeTierCaps: Unlimited base resumes; 2 tailored resumes, 2 application packets, 100 tracked jobs and 100 document uploads
pricing.hiddenCosts: The lower advertised effective rates require $90 quarterly or $160 six-month prepayment; there is no annual billing option.

verdictSummary: The core loop is small enough for a capable coding agent to produce a useful local version in one sitting. For Huntr, track job applications, contacts, tasks, documents, and tailored materials in one workspace. The hard boundary is browser capture, ai writing, resume builder, contact enrichment, and sync, plus data, distribution, and coaching.
coreLoopDIY: Track job applications, contacts, tasks, and documents in one workspace, tailor user-authored materials against a supplied role, and keep every claim traceable to the user's own evidence.
whatYouLose: browser capture, AI writing, resume builder, contact enrichment, and sync
ongoingBurden: document parsing, truthful claim handling, job-source changes, browser automation rules, privacy, model drift, and user review
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Huntr because people pay for convenience, curated guidance, and distribution; the personal tracking and drafting loop is highly buildable. The recurring cost buys document parsing, truthful claim handling, job-source changes, browser automation rules, privacy, model drift, and user review, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Reactive Resume
priorArt.desc: Active open-source resume builder with structured data and PDF export.

alternatives.name: Reactive Resume
alternatives.desc: A credible job-search workspace: applications, contacts, tasks, files, resumes and cover letters all live together.

alternatives.name: JobSync
alternatives.desc: A self-hosted application tracker with tasks, documents and activity history, minus Huntr's polished contact CRM.

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Pro plan and a personal job-search workspace DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a personal replacement for Huntr in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and an optional OpenAI API; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: track job applications, contacts, tasks, and documents in one workspace, tailor user-authored materials against a supplied role, and keep every claim traceable to the user's own evidence.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a structured evidence bank for roles, projects, skills, dates, metrics, and source notes.
Import a job description and highlight requirements without inventing missing experience.
Generate a tailored resume variant only from approved evidence and show the source for each bullet.
Add application stages, contacts, tasks, dates, notes, documents, and a follow-up view.
Provide interview-question practice with answer notes and a self-review rubric, not deceptive live assistance.
Export resume data as JSON and PDF plus the application tracker as CSV.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Deliberately leave out automatic mass application.
Deliberately leave out fabricated qualifications or deceptive interview assistance.
Deliberately leave out proprietary recruiter databases and guaranteed job outcomes.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
